pipeline.title: REST API Pipeline System
pipeline.subtitle: Efficient Management of Interconnected API Call Chains
pipeline.description: A powerful system for organizing sequential HTTP requests to REST API, where each subsequent call can utilize data from the previous one. Provides complete control over request chain execution with progress visualization and intelligent error handling.

sequential_chains.title: Sequential HTTP chains
sequential_chains.description: System organizes and executes REST API requests strictly one after another, ensuring correct execution order and control over data flow.

auto_data_transfer.title: Auto data transfer between steps
auto_data_transfer.description: Results of each executed request (e.g., created object ID) are automatically and safely substituted into parameters of subsequent requests, eliminating manual data stitching.

realtime_progress.title: Real-time progress tracking
realtime_progress.description: Interface displays visual progress bar and status of each stage, providing user with full transparency about current execution state.

error_handling.title: Smart error handling and retries
error_handling.description: System analyzes server response codes (e.g., 5xx errors) and automatically performs request retries according to configurable rules, increasing fault tolerance.

conditional_logic.title: Conditional execution logic
conditional_logic.description: Allows defining rules (e.g., if/else) that determine whether the next request will be executed, based on data obtained in previous steps.

auto_cancel.title: Auto-cancel dependent requests
auto_cancel.description: When a fatal error occurs, the system automatically aborts execution of the entire subsequent chain, preventing pointless calls.

type_safety.title: End-to-end type safety
type_safety.description: Thanks to TypeScript integration, system ensures strict type checking for input parameters and data passed between pipeline steps.

restMonitoring.title: REST API Monitoring Module

restMonitoring.description: A built-in module for real-time REST API health monitoring: accumulates HTTP request history, builds per-endpoint analytics, tracks errors with trend comparison, and sends Telegram alerts when configurable threshold rules are triggered.

error_tracking.title: Error Tracking with Delta

endpoint_probing.title: Active Endpoint Probing

telegram_alerts.title: Rule-Based Telegram Alerts

deployPlatform.title: Vue/Nuxt Application Auto-Deploy and Hosting Platform
deployPlatform.subtitle: Dynamic Hosting with Auto-Build, Domains and TLS
deployPlatform.description: A lifecycle management system for Vue and Nuxt applications: clones the repository, builds the image in an isolated container with memory limits, publishes the result behind Traefik with automatic TLS, and binds any custom domain — all through a control panel, without editing configs or SSH.

auto_build.title: Automatic Build from Repository
auto_build.description: On deploy command the system clones the target branch (including private repositories) and runs the build in an ephemeral Docker container with the specified Node version, dependency install, and build commands.

multi_type.title: Vue SPA, Nuxt Static and Nuxt SSR Support
multi_type.description: For each application type the deployer generates an appropriate Dockerfile: static apps are packed into an nginx image, SSR into a Node image with a live process on port 3000.

dynamic_routing.title: Dynamic Domain Routing
dynamic_routing.description: Adding an application in the panel automatically attaches Traefik labels to the container. A new domain becomes active without restarting the gateway or editing configuration files.

auto_tls.title: Automatic TLS (Let's Encrypt)
auto_tls.description: Traefik requests and renews Let's Encrypt certificates via HTTP-01 on first access to the domain. Certificate status is shown in the application card in the control panel.

private_repos.title: Private Repositories with Encrypted Tokens
private_repos.description: SSH deploy keys or personal tokens are stored encrypted in the database (AES-256-GCM), decrypted only during cloning, and never appear in logs.

resource_limits.title: Production Protection from OOM During Build
resource_limits.description: Every build container is launched with an explicit memory limit and NODE_OPTIONS; builds run strictly one at a time in a queue — peak Vite/Nuxt consumption cannot crash running production services.

items.name: Deployer Service
items.description: deploy orchestrator inside the API: clones the repository, generates a Dockerfile for the application type, runs the build, and starts the container

items.name: Build Queue
items.description: build queue with concurrent run locking that protects server resources from overload

items.description: encrypted storage of SSH keys and tokens for accessing private repositories

pipeline-demo.title: Pipeline Demo
pipeline-demo.intro_problem: When working with a complex REST API, data for one request depends on the result of another. The code gets cluttered with nested async calls, scattered constants, and manual parameter passing. Such code is hard to read, test, and maintain.
pipeline-demo.intro_solution: Rest Pipeline JS offers an elegant solution. It's a library that turns a chaotic chain of requests into a logical, sequential pipeline. You describe the steps, and the mechanism takes care of data preparation, request execution, and response/error handling.
pipeline-demo.intro_example: How does it work? Let's look at the example of booking a flight:
pipeline-demo.intro_declarative: You simply describe 'what' needs to be done, not 'how' to implement it technically. All data flow logic is encapsulated in a declarative pipeline.
pipeline-demo.intro_spaghetti: Turn spaghetti code of async requests into a neat and reliable pipeline. With Rest Pipeline JS, working with complex APIs becomes easy.
pipeline-demo.step_route_desc: The pipeline requests the entire flight network and automatically selects a random direction.
pipeline-demo.step_flight_desc: Gets the list of available flights for the selected route and picks the nearest one by date.
pipeline-demo.step_services_desc: Loads available services for the flight and adds several options to the booking.
pipeline-demo.step_seat_desc: Requests the cabin layout and reserves a random free seat.
pipeline-demo.feature1_desc: rest-pipeline-js allows you to build complex pipelines from sequential steps for working with REST APIs. Each step can have its own parameters, execution conditions, error handlers, and dependencies, providing maximum flexibility for integration with any service.
pipeline-demo.feature2_desc: The module supports progress tracking, event subscription (success, error, log), and extension via before, after, errorHandler hooks. This enables complex scenarios, logging, error handling, and dynamic process management.
pipeline-demo.feature3_desc: Each step can specify retryCount, timeoutMs, caching parameters, and rate limits. This makes working with unstable or slow APIs reliable and manageable, reducing errors and speeding up data processing.
pipeline-demo.feature4_desc: rest-pipeline-js provides ready-to-use composition functions for Vue 3 and hooks for React, making it easy to integrate pipeline logic into modern frontend apps. You get reactive progress, statuses, logs, and step management right in the component.
pipeline-demo.step1: Request the flight network and select a random pair of departure and arrival points.
pipeline-demo.step2: Get the list of available flights for the selected route and choose a random flight for the nearest date.
pipeline-demo.step3: Request the list of services for the selected flight and choose several random available services.
pipeline-demo.step4: Get the seat map for the selected flight and choose a random free seat in the aircraft cabin.
